record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.original_question: For each gl-regular Nijenhuis operator in dimension 2 from the known list of explicit normal forms, describe all conservation laws, or at least construct one regular conservation law for each operator, including at singular points where the eigenvalues collide.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.3. We have a complete classification of gl-regular Nijenhuis operators in dimension 2 as a list of explicit normal forms. Describe all conservation laws for each of these operators. Or at least, find one regular conservation law for each of them.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let M be a smooth two-dimensional manifold and let L: TM → TM be a (1,1)-tensor field (Nijenhuis operator) whose Nijenhuis torsion

  N_L(X,Y) := L^2[X,Y] - L[LX,Y] - L[X,LY] + [LX,LY]

vanishes identically. Assume that L is gl-regular, i.e. at every point p ∈ M the operator L_p has a cyclic vector (equivalently, the minimal and characteristic polynomials of L_p coincide). A function f ∈ C^∞(M) is called a conservation law of L if the 1-form d(L^* df) is symmetric, equivalently L^* df is closed, where L^* denotes the dual operator acting on 1-forms; a conservation law is called regular if df ≠ 0 at the point under consideration.

It is known that in dimension 2 the gl-regular Nijenhuis operators admit a complete classification by a list of explicit local normal forms, including at singular points where the two eigenvalues of L collide.

Problem. For each operator L appearing in this list of explicit normal forms of two-dimensional gl-regular Nijenhuis operators:
(a) describe the space of all (local) conservation laws of L; or at least
(b) exhibit one regular conservation law of L,
including a description valid at the singular points where the eigenvalues coincide.
artifact.status_search_result: Conservation laws and symmetries of gl-regular Nijenhuis operators have been systematically studied in the "Nijenhuis geometry IV" work (arXiv:2304.10626), which establishes a splitting theorem and shows that all conservation laws can be obtained from a single one via multiplication by symmetries. Explicit normal forms in dimension 2 are classified in "Nijenhuis geometry III" (arXiv:2007.09506). However, a complete case-by-case description of all conservation laws for every normal form in dimension 2, especially at singular points where the eigenvalues collide, does not appear to be fully carried out in the literature, so the problem appears partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis geometry IV: conservation laws, symmetries and integration
status_evidence.snippet: Study of symmetries and conservation laws of gl-regular Nijenhuis operators; splitting theorem; any conservation law arises from a single one via multiplication by a symmetry.
status_evidence.claim: General theory of conservation laws of gl-regular Nijenhuis operators is developed, providing partial answer.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis geometry III: gl-regular Nijenhuis operators
status_evidence.snippet: Provides explicit normal forms of gl-regular Nijenhuis operators, including in dimension 2 near singular points.
status_evidence.claim: Normal forms list referenced in the problem is established.
